seoTitle: Free GitHub Actions Matrix Builder Online
metaDescription: Free online GitHub Actions matrix builder. Describe os and version dimensions with include and exclude rows and get a ready workflow file.
intro: Describe matrix dimensions such as os and node version, add include and exclude rows, and get a complete GitHub Actions workflow with strategy.matrix, setup action and test command.
why:
Testing across several operating systems and language versions is easy to want and awkward to write. The matrix syntax has its own rules for include and exclude, and a small indentation slip changes which jobs run. Many projects end up with a matrix nobody dares touch.

Write each dimension as a line, for example os: ubuntu-latest, windows-latest or node: 20, 22, then add exclude or include lines with key=value pairs. The tool builds a workflow with checkout, the right setup action for your language, install and test commands, fail-fast and max-parallel settings, and continue-on-error for experimental rows. It shows what the matrix will contain, but not how many jobs your plan allows, so keep an eye on total job count. Nothing is uploaded.
howTo: Write dimensions as name: value, value, one per line.
Add exclude and include lines using key=value pairs.
Choose the setup action for your language, and edit the install and test commands.
Set fail-fast, max-parallel and branch, then copy the workflow.

faq.q: How do include and exclude work?
faq.a: Exclude removes a combination from the generated matrix, for example macOS with Node 20. Include adds extra combinations or extra variables, such as an experimental Node 24 job on Ubuntu.
Setup actions for Node, Python, Go, Java, Ruby and .NET, or none if you only want the matrix. Each has default install and test commands you can override.

faq.q: What does the experimental key do?
faq.a: If any include row sets experimental=true, the job gets continue-on-error based on that value, so a failure in an experimental job does not fail the whole run.

faq.q: Does it count jobs for me?
faq.a: No. Multiply the values in each dimension, subtract excludes and add includes to estimate the number of jobs, and check your plan limits.
